stagedRequirements.originalRequirementText: The system must support associating enhancements, allegations, priors, and other modifiers to specific offenses (charges) and at the case level, based on configurable court rules.

sourceReviewerNotes.note: 3/17/26 AI review: Based on the conversation in the meeting, I think this requirement is fine.

Amendments, deleting and adding new charges.  3/20/26 We have this ability in 3 places. On ADDTRCR when the case is built. On UPDTCJ after the case is added so other charges can be added with this criteria and on the AMEND screen after a hearing.  there may be some parts of this available in Docket, but can't say for sure.  Just want to clarify if this ability will be available in multiple places considering the phases of the case.

3/20:  After our discussion, I believe this requirement is fine as-is.  

My understanding of the required fields in the statute table: effective begin and end dates, offense types (fel,msd,inf), statute descriptions, triggers that indicate if the offense can have a jail term affixed as a judgment, if an abstract needs sent to DMV in a batch report, and to notify DMV if the statute is eligible for a suspended license.  If the statute is a speeding offense, we must track location and where the speeding range is.  Additionally we also collect the AAMVA codes which tell DMV how many points should be taken from the driver record- it would be nice if DMV could update some of these fields themselves.   We also collect the PCH charge from NSP, and collect the statute chapter.  

I believe a lot of judges would like the ability for our CMS to better match the statutes as they are listed by the legislative website. 

We should add a requirement that collection of these items should be set at the state-level and at the county level for court clerks to maintain their county ordinances for city prosecutor charges.
I was thinking about the same as Laurayne on the multiple areas where information is amended and must be recorded to other screens
